subject: Archaeology
title: The Chauvet Cave: Art Before Civilization
description: A 60-second lesson on The Chauvet Cave: Art Before Civilization.

hook.text: Cave paintings in southern France are 36,000 years old — twice as old as Lascaux — and far more sophisticated.

buildup.text: Chauvet Cave was discovered in 1994 by three hikers. Lions, rhinos, and bears cover the walls in dynamic poses.

discovery.text: Artists used shading, perspective, and even motion lines. One panel shows a bison with eight legs to suggest running.

twist.text: The cave had been sealed by a rockfall 20,000 years ago. The air inside was untouched, the art pristine.

climax.text: Chauvet proves that artistic genius did not evolve gradually. Full sophistication appeared right from the start.

punchline.text: The oldest known art is also among the best.

quiz.question: What makes Chauvet Cave art surprising to researchers?
options: It uses metal pigments not found in later cave art
It shows full artistic sophistication from the very start, not gradual improvement
It depicts scenes of farming that predate known agriculture
